chapter: Woody Herman, Henderson and the Indiana Theater
title: A walk-in composer and the China Boy arrangement for Henderson
summary: A young songwriter had Randolph score a big-band arrangement that Henderson played, and Henderson then asked for three China arrangements, of which Randolph did China Boy.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Speaking about arranging, I managed to get a chance to arrange for Fletcher, fellow just came in off the streets, their names were -- what was that-- Mary told my wife, he said, my name is -- his name was Martin, because I remember, when she said, Oh, Martin, he says, Miz

Randolph, my name is not Martin, my name is Martine. So now, his name is Martine, and he came in and he wanted to hear a number that he had composed. And I took the lead down for him and made out his copyright, made out his lead sheet and fixed out the copyright blank for him. He says, now I want you to fix me an arrangement for it. I say, well, what kind of arrangement do you want me to fix? He says, fix me a nice dance arrangement on it. I said, how big arrangement? He said, bigband. I said, okay, a big band. So I fixed a big band arrangement, and gave it to him.

He carried it down to the Grand Terrace to Fletcher. And Fletcher said, would you play this arrangement? So Fletcher told him, yes, I'll play it. And Fletcher played it, and when he played the arrangement, it was hitting. Fletcher says, do you know where this guy lives? That made this arrangement? He says, yeah, I see him every day. Say, tell him to call me.

So he told me, he says, Fletcher -- says, Mr. Randolph? I said, What? Fletcher Henderson say call him, I say, okay. but I didn't think much of it. I didn't call him. So finally (unintelligible), so I saw him again. He said, look, I saw Fletcher again, Fletcher bawled me out. He said -- I said, Okay, I'll call him. Because Fletcher told him that he didn't tell me. Well, I called him and I told (unintelligible) he said, did you get my message? I said, yes, that boy told me, but I was busy and I didn't really have time. That's

what I told him. He said, well, I want to get you to make the three arrangements for me, three China arrangements. I said, Yes? He said, You know them? I said, China Boy. He says, Yes. I said, Chinatown, and he says, Yes, I said, I don't know that other one. And Fletcher said, China Girl.
Well, I didn't know there was a China Girl, did you?
I've seen the title somewhere. I've never heard the tune.

Yeah. Well, I got as far as China Boy, because something came up and I didn't get a chance to make the others. What? I had to go to New York, that's what it was. I had to go to New York with Woody. That's what it was. But I made China Boy for him. Yeah, China Boy. Wait a minute. I get mixed up on those Chinas now.
(Musical sounds.) Well, I don't know how they come out. I know he rehearsed the band on it. And then I had to go to New York to join Woody.
You said Paul Edward Miller was involved in your getting with Woody.
Yes, he certainly was. Paul was a
nice boy, he was a nice fellow.
